security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU retains writable SPTTCD (bit 24) and MPTTCD (bit 42) fields in mstatus/sstatus/vsstatus after the Zitagelide extension is removed, allowing guests to write to bits that the current spec defines as WPRI (read-only zero). Additionally, if the TTCD state machinery (spill on trap, restore on mret/sret) is not removed, stale or attacker-controlled TTCD values could influence tag check enforcement on memory accesses.
security_spec.summary: Removal of Zitagelide renders SPTTCD (mstatus/sstatus bit 24) and MPTTCD (mstatus bit 42) as WPRI — QEMU must hardwire these bits to zero and remove all TTCD state spill/restore logic to prevent guest info leaks through now-reserved CSR fields
